A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SG-I2V and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Corresponding content can be reliably matched despite the added appendix and revised presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original VIPSeg evaluations, qualitative video-generation results, feature analyses, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds MOFT comparison results, a Gaussian-weighting ablation, and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: The feature alignment, Gaussian-weighted latent optimization, and frequency-preserving post-processing remain the same. v3 clarifies that attention modification applies only during loss computation. Its corrected Equation (2) matches the procedure already described in v1's prose and Figure 3.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate on VIPSeg validation and demonstrate object, part, nonphysical-entity, and camera motion control. Figure 1 replaces individual qualitative examples without establishing a new dataset, task, or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds the adapted MOFT baseline, using features derived through Content Correlation Removal. All previous comparators remain. Specifying DragNUWA as v1.5 clarifies its version rather than establishing a different comparator.

E3.justification: New Table 2 introduces identity weighting as a control against Gaussian weighting. The main SVD configuration and stated optimization schedule remain unchanged. Appendix A newly documents metric resizing and evaluation exclusions; it does not establish changes to the previously reported experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a Gaussian-versus-identity weighting ablation, testing whether emphasizing bounding-box centers improves generation and trajectory fidelity. Existing feature, layer, frequency-cutoff, learning-rate, and timestep analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds MOFT results: FID 30.76, FVD 402.09, and ObjMC 33.58. All existing rows remain unchanged, including SG-I2V's 28.87/298.10/14.43. Table 2 adds identity-weighting results of 28.88/300.20/14.72. v3 also replaces some Figure 1 examples and newly reports runtime and memory usage.

T1.justification: Equation (2) changes the high-frequency term from the optimized latent z_t* to the original latent z_t. This fixes an expression that previously combined complementary frequencies from the same optimized latent, making it consistent with the stated restoration procedure. No new proofs or theoretical results appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list qualify 'competitive with supervised models' to 'significantly narrowing down the performance gap.' The central claims of zero-shot, self-guided trajectory control and superiority over adapted zero-shot baselines remain.

C2.justification: v3 explains Gaussian weighting as reducing unwanted background movement and discusses why MOFT features are unsuitable without reference motion. Section 4.4 newly attributes misleading late-timestep ObjMC improvements to tracking moving artifacts. Figure 4 is explicitly framed as supervised-baseline failure cases; the existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands reproducibility information: FVD resizing to 256×256, ObjMC processing at 320×576, Co-Tracker v2, excluded out-of-frame points and short videos, and adapted-baseline implementation details. Appendix C adds A6000 48GB hardware, average runtime of 305 seconds, and roughly 30GB peak memory. These are new disclosures rather than demonstrated revisions to existing settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds TraDiffusion and DragEntity citations and expands the relationship to MOFT through comparison and discussion. MOFT's underlying Xiao et al. work was already cited in v1. The broader positioning relative to supervised control and tuning-free generation remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and most prose remain intact. Changes include localized explanatory rewrites, acknowledgements, the conference header, and a new experimental-details Appendix A that shifts the former Appendices A/B to B/C.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces selected examples, Figure 3 is redrawn, and Figure 4's caption is revised. Table 1 gains a MOFT row and Table 2 is added. The remaining figures and quantitative plots are retained, with limited layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility and interpretation through detailed evaluation and baseline documentation, corrected Equation (2), computational-cost reporting, and a targeted ablation. The qualified supervised comparison and artifact-tracking explanation also improve calibration while the main results remain unchanged. These benefits outweigh small inconsistencies, including Appendix C's 75 optimization iterations versus the 80 implied by the retained inclusive 45–30 schedule at five iterations per timestep.
